title: Guess These 3 Indian States From Their Shape 🗺️

beats.say: Three Indian states, shapes only. One is eighty-three times another's size.
beats.caption: 3 states · shapes only · one is ~83× another

beats.say: Shape one: second-largest state in the last census. Which is it?
beats.caption: Shape 1 · 2nd largest (Census 2011) · Which state?

beats.say: Madhya Pradesh, ahead of Maharashtra by five hundred and thirty-nine square kilometres.
beats.caption: MADHYA PRADESH · ahead of Maharashtra by 539 km²

beats.say: Shape two gained four taluks from Travancore-Cochin in nineteen fifty-six. Which is it?
beats.caption: Shape 2 · 1956: four taluks moved in · Which state?

beats.say: Tamil Nadu, then called Madras. Those taluks became Kanyakumari district.
beats.caption: TAMIL NADU (then Madras) · Kanyakumari: 1,684 km² (2011)

beats.say: Shape three: so small, we had to zoom in. Which is it?
beats.caption: Shape 3 · zoomed in · Which state?

beats.say: Goa, the smallest state by area in the last census.
beats.caption: GOA · smallest state by area (Census 2011)

beats.say: Shape one is about eighty-three Goas. How many did you get?
beats.caption: Madhya Pradesh ≈ 83 × Goa (Census 2011 areas)

wording_notes: 'in the last census' for every rank
Tamil Nadu drawn alone, without Puducherry
1,684 km² credited to Census 2011, not Survey of India
house outline is today's MP, never the 1956 shape
